text: Q claims constant-factor approximation to FIRST-BEST GFT (not second-best) for XOS buyer + additive seller with independent items. This is unusually strong - most bilateral trade results target second-best. Q uses "simple mechanisms" (likely sequential posted prices). P studies LLM agents negotiating contracts in CT game (spatial-temporal bargaining + navigation). Key tension: Q is mechanism design (direct revelation, centralized), P is contract negotiation (decentralized bargaining). Abstract scan hypothesis conflates these paradigms.

Q is mechanism design: centralized direct-revelation mechanisms achieving constant-factor approximation to FIRST-BEST GFT (not second-best) for XOS buyer + additive seller, satisfying BIC/IIR/ex-ante WBB. P is contract-theoretic bargaining: LLM agents negotiate/enforce contracts in CT spatial-temporal game (navigation + trading). Critical mismatch: Q assumes truthful reporting to mechanism; P studies strategic negotiation between agents. The hypothesis "implement Qs mechanism in Ps framework" conflates paradigms. sharper question: can P-style LLM negotiators approximate Qs GFT guarantees when trading multidimensional items, without a centralized mechanism?
